library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aoki_2017_asthma_fev1_placebo"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aoki_2017_asthma_fev1_placebo"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-017-9550-0>

Aoki 2017 is a methods paper on model selection and model averaging for
Phase IIb dose selection. Its simulation studies are built on one fitted
population model: a placebo model of clinic FEV1 in asthma, estimated from
the placebo and lowest-dose (AZD1981 10 mg twice daily) arms of the AZD1981
Phase IIb trial. That placebo model is the model packaged here. The paper's
four candidate dose-effect functions (linear, log-linear, Emax and sigmoid
Emax) are used only to simulate and re-estimate artificial drug effects; no
AZD1981 drug-effect estimate is reported, so none is packaged. The last
section of this article shows how the paper adds those simulated effects to
the placebo model.

# Population

The model was fit to 324 adults with inadequately controlled atopic asthma
(1,803 clinic FEV1 measurements) from the placebo and AZD1981 10 mg twice
daily arms of the 12-week, multicentre AZD1981 Phase IIb trial
(NCT01197794). The two arms were pooled as a "placebo" dataset because they
did not differ significantly, and dosing records were not supplied to the
authors. FEV1 was measured at seven clinic visits two weeks apart: visit 1
was screening, visit 2 the baseline, and visits 3 to 7 followed
randomization.

Aoki 2017 does not tabulate demographics. The trial report (Bateman 2018,
<https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S147389>) gives them by arm. Pooling its
placebo and 10 mg columns (Table 1) gives a mean age of about 45 years,
49.8% female, and 72.0% White, 17.5% Asian, 1.2% Black and 9.2% other.
Inclusion required a prebronchodilator FEV1 of 40-85% of predicted normal,
at least 12% reversibility, a positive Phadiatop test and an ACQ5 score of
at least 1, on budesonide/formoterol maintenance therapy. The trial ran in
Europe, South and North America, Japan and South Africa.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Aoki_2017_asthma_fev1_placebo")$population`.

# Source trace

The placebo-model equation in the Models section of Aoki 2017:

$$
\mathrm{FEV1} = \left(\mathrm{FEV1}_{\mathrm{Baseline}} +
\begin{cases} 0 & \text{visit} = 1, 2 \\ \mathrm{FEV1}_{\mathrm{Placebo}} & \text{visit} = 3, \ldots, 7 \end{cases}\right)(1 + \epsilon_1) + \epsilon_2
$$

$$
\mathrm{FEV1}_{\mathrm{Placebo}} = \theta_1 + \eta_1, \qquad
\mathrm{FEV1}_{\mathrm{Baseline}} = \theta_2 e^{\eta_2}
\left(1 + \theta_3 (\mathrm{FEV1\%N} - \overline{\mathrm{FEV1\%N}})\right)
\left(1 + \theta_4 (\mathrm{Age} - \overline{\mathrm{Age}})\right)
\begin{cases} 1 & \text{male} \\ \theta_5 & \text{female} \end{cases}
$$

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---------------|------:|-----------------|
| `plbmax` (theta1, placebo effect) | 0.169 L | Table 1 (RSE 11.9%) |
| `lrbase` (theta2, baseline FEV1, male at reference covariates) | log(2.51 L) | Table 1 (RSE 0.828%) |
| `e_fev1_pctpred_rbase` (theta3, FEV1 % of normal) | 0.0129 per % | Table 1 (RSE 3.87%); printed unit "L^-1" |
| `e_age_rbase` (theta4, age) | -0.0105 1/year | Table 1 (RSE 5.01%) |
| `e_sexf_rbase` (theta5, female factor) | 0.719 | Table 1 (RSE 1.43%) |
| `etaplbmax` (omega1, additive IIV on the placebo effect) | SD 0.303 L, variance 0.0918 | Table 1 (RSE 8.88%) |
| `etalrbase` (omega2, exponential IIV on baseline) | SD 0.105, variance 0.0110 | Table 1 (RSE 5.97%) |
| `propSd_FEV1` (sigma1, proportional RUV) | 0.0832 | Table 1 (RSE 7.60%) |
| `addSd_FEV1` (sigma2, additive RUV) | 0.102 L | Table 1 (RSE 18.8%) |
| Step function of visit for the placebo effect | -- | Models section, placebo-model equation and the paragraph comparing it with Wang et al. 2012 |
| Combined error `(1 + eps1) + eps2` | -- | Placebo-model equation |
| Reference FEV1 % of normal = 62.5% | -- | Not printed; midpoint of the 40-85% inclusion range (Bateman 2018 Methods) |
| Reference age = 45 years | -- | Not printed; rounded mean of the placebo and 10 mg arms (Bateman 2018 Table 1) |

The covariate in the paper is "the percentage of FEV1 at visit 2 compared to
the predicted normal", i.e. the baseline FEV1 % predicted, which the model
takes as the time-fixed column `FEV1_PCTPRED`.

# Typical-value checks

With the random effects zeroed, the model is a closed-form expression. The
solve below checks it against that expression, element by element, for a
male and a female patient at the reference covariates and for patients
10 years older or 10 percentage points higher in FEV1 % predicted. Time is
weeks since the baseline visit; the baseline (`time = 0`) carries no placebo
effect and every later visit carries all of it.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Aoki_2017_asthma_fev1_placebo")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

profiles <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~label,                           ~SEXF, ~AGE, ~FEV1_PCTPRED,
  1L,  "Male, reference covariates",       0,     45,   62.5,
  2L,  "Female, reference covariates",     1,     45,   62.5,
  3L,  "Male, age 55 years",               0,     55,   62.5,
  4L,  "Male, FEV1 72.5% predicted",       0,     45,   72.5
)

ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(profiles, time = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time)

# zeroRe() leaves the etas declared at zero variance; rxode2 notes that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is intended for a typical-value solve.
sim_typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typ, ev_typ,
    keep = c("label", "SEXF", "AGE", "FEV1_PCTPRED")
  )),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
)

expected <- with(sim_typ,
  2.51 * (1 + 0.0129 * (FEV1_PCTPRED - 62.5)) * (1 - 0.0105 * (AGE - 45)) *
    ifelse(SEXF == 1, 0.719, 1) + ifelse(time > 0, 0.169, 0)
)
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is pure arithmetic.
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_typ$FEV1 - expected)) < 1e-8)

sim_typ |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 2)) |>
  mutate(visit = ifelse(time == 0, "Baseline (visit 2)", "Post-baseline (visits 3-7)")) |>
  select(label, visit, FEV1) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = visit, values_from = FEV1) |>
  dplyr::rename("Patient" = label) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical FEV1 (L) by patient profile.")
```

The female factor gives a baseline of 2.51 x 0.719 = 1.805 L, ten years of
age lower the baseline by 10.5%, and ten points of FEV1 % predicted raise it
by 12.9%. The typical placebo effect adds 0.169 L at every post-baseline
visit.

# Virtual cohort

The cohort approximates the analysed trial population. Age is drawn from a
normal distribution with the pooled mean of 45.4 years and an assumed SD of
13 years, redrawn until it lies in 18-80 years. Baseline FEV1 % predicted is
uniform over the 40-85% inclusion range, and 49.8% of patients are female.
Visits 3 to 7 are placed at weeks 2 to 10 after the baseline visit.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20171101)
n_subj <- 200L

draw_age <- function(n, mean = 45.4, sd = 13, lo = 18, hi = 80) {
  out <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    out[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  }
  out
}

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_subj),
  AGE = draw_age(n_subj),
  FEV1_PCTPRED = runif(n_subj, 40, 85),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_subj, 1, 0.498)
)

visits <- tibble::tibble(visit = 2:7, time = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10))

ev_vpc <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, visits) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20171101)
simdf <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, ev_vpc,
  keep = c("visit", "AGE", "FEV1_PCTPRED", "SEXF")
))
if (is.null(simdf$id)) simdf$id <- 1L
```

The simulated FEV1 by visit, with the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles across
the cohort:

```{r vpc-plot}
vpc <- simdf |>
  group_by(visit) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(simdf, aes(visit, sim)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_ribbon(data = vpc, aes(x = visit, ymin = p05, ymax = p95), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = vpc, aes(visit, p50), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:7) +
  labs(x = "Visit (2 = baseline)", y = "Simulated FEV1 (L)",
       title = "Simulated clinic FEV1 under placebo",
       caption = "Lines: individual patients; band: 5th-95th percentile; thick line: median.")
```

# Placebo-effect validation

The paper motivates the case study by FEV1 being highly variable relative to
the 0.1 L target effect, with "standard deviation of 0.3 L in the placebo
effect", which is the estimated omega1 = 0.303 L. The individual placebo
effect `plbi` in the simulation should therefore centre on 0.169 L with a
between-patient SD near 0.30 L. The observed change from baseline, the
average of visits 3-7 minus visit 2 as in the trial's primary analysis,
should centre on the same 0.169 L.

```{r placebo-check}
per_subj <- simdf |>
  group_by(id, SEXF) |>
  summarise(
    plbi = first(plbi),
    rbase = first(rbase),
    cfb = mean(sim[visit >= 3]) - sim[visit == 2],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

chk <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Median individual placebo effect (L)",
               "SD of individual placebo effect (L)",
               "Median observed change from baseline, visits 3-7 (L)"),
  Simulated = c(median(per_subj$plbi), sd(per_subj$plbi), median(per_subj$cfb)),
  Paper = c(0.169, 0.303, 0.169)
)
knitr::kable(chk, digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Centre: the SE of a 200-subject median is about 0.027 L for plbi (SD 0.30 L)
  # and about 0.034 L for the observed change, which also carries residual
  # error (SD about 0.38 L). The bounds sit at 3.5 SE or more and still catch a
  # mis-signed theta1 (off by 0.34 L) or a decimal slip (0.0169 or 1.69).
  abs(median(per_subj$plbi) - 0.169) < 0.1,
  abs(median(per_subj$cfb) - 0.169) < 0.12,
  # Spread: the SD of a 200-subject sample is within about 15% of omega1 at
  # three SE; a variance entered as an SD (0.303 vs 0.092) or vice versa
  # fails by a factor of three.
  sd(per_subj$plbi) > 0.2,
  sd(per_subj$plbi) < 0.4
)
```

The baseline is log-normal around the covariate-adjusted typical value, and
female patients have a baseline about 28% lower than male patients:

```{r baseline-check}
per_subj |>
  mutate(Sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male")) |>
  group_by(Sex) |>
  summarise(N = n(), `Median baseline FEV1 (L)` = median(rbase), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# The paper's simulated drug effects

To build its simulation studies the paper adds an artificial drug effect to
the placebo data. For each simulated trial the theoretical minimum effective
dose (tMED, the dose giving exactly 0.1 L) is drawn uniformly within a range
(Table 2), and the dose-effect parameters are chosen so that the function
passes through 0.1 L at tMED:

* log-linear, `p1 * log(1 + p2 * dose)`: `DE(1000 mg) ~ U(0.2, 0.3)` and `DE(tMED) = 0.1`;
* Emax, `EMAX * dose / (EC50 + dose)`: `EMAX ~ U(0.2, 0.3)` and `DE(tMED) = 0.1`;
* sigmoid Emax: as Emax with `gamma ~ U(0.5, 4)`.

The chunk below reproduces the construction of Figure 5 (Simulation Study 3,
tMED between 40 and 100 mg). These functions are not part of the packaged
model.

```{r figure5}
set.seed(5)
n_curves <- 10L
dose_grid <- exp(seq(log(1), log(1000), length.out = 120))

make_loglinear <- function(tmed, de1000) {
  # Solve p1 * log(1 + p2 * 1000) = de1000 and p1 * log(1 + p2 * tmed) = 0.1.
  ratio <- function(lp2) log(1 + exp(lp2) * 1000) / log(1 + exp(lp2) * tmed) - de1000 / 0.1
  p2 <- exp(uniroot(ratio, c(-30, 30))$root)
  p1 <- 0.1 / log(1 + p2 * tmed)
  function(dose) p1 * log(1 + p2 * dose)
}
make_emax <- function(tmed, emax, gamma = 1) {
  ec50 <- tmed * (emax / 0.1 - 1)^(1 / gamma)
  function(dose) emax * dose^gamma / (ec50^gamma + dose^gamma)
}

curves <- list()
tmeds <- list()
for (i in seq_len(n_curves)) {
  tmed <- runif(3, 40, 100)
  fns <- list(
    `Log-linear` = make_loglinear(tmed[1], runif(1, 0.2, 0.3)),
    Emax = make_emax(tmed[2], runif(1, 0.2, 0.3)),
    `Sigmoid Emax` = make_emax(tmed[3], runif(1, 0.2, 0.3), runif(1, 0.5, 4))
  )
  for (k in seq_along(fns)) {
    curves[[length(curves) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      curve = paste(names(fns)[k], i), family = names(fns)[k],
      dose = dose_grid, effect = fns[[k]](dose_grid)
    )
    tmeds[[length(tmeds) + 1L]] <- fns[[k]](tmed[k])
  }
}
curves <- bind_rows(curves)

# Every curve passes through the target effect at its own tMED by construction.
stopifnot(max(abs(unlist(tmeds) - 0.1)) < 1e-6)

ggplot(curves, aes(dose, effect, group = curve, colour = family)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(40, 100), linetype = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Drug effect on FEV1 (L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Simulated dose-effect curves, Simulation Study 3",
       caption = "Replicates the construction of Figure 5 of Aoki 2017 (tMED between 40 and 100 mg).")
```

In the paper's estimation models the chosen function `DE_j(dose)` enters the
placebo model as `FEV1 = Baseline + PlaceboEffect + DE_j` at the
post-baseline visits, inside the same combined residual error.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Centring values.** The paper centres FEV1 % of normal and age on the
  population means of its dataset but does not print them, and neither does
  the trial report. The maintainers used 62.5% predicted (the midpoint of the
  40-85% inclusion range) and 45 years (the 45.4-year mean of the placebo and
  10 mg arms in Bateman 2018 Table 1, rounded). With the published
  coefficients, a 1-point error in the FEV1 % reference moves the typical
  baseline by 1.3%, and a 1-year error in the age reference moves it by 1.05%.
  A user with the actual means can rescale `lrbase` accordingly.
* **Unit of theta3.** Table 1 prints the FEV1 % of normal coefficient as
  "0.0129 L^-1". In the printed equation it multiplies a difference of
  percentages inside a dimensionless factor, so the model treats it as per
  percentage point.
* **Time axis.** The paper's placebo effect is a step in visit number. The
  model uses time in weeks since the baseline visit (visit 2) and applies the
  placebo effect at every `time > 0`. The screening visit (visit 1) also
  carries no placebo effect; simulate it as a second `time = 0` record if
  needed. The paper says FEV1 was measured every 2 weeks over the 12-week
  study, so this article places visits 3-7 at weeks 2-10; the predictions do
  not depend on that choice.
* **Demographics.** Aoki 2017 gives no demographic table. Age, sex and race in
  the `population` metadata come from Bateman 2018 Table 1, whose placebo and
  10 mg columns add up to 325 patients against the 324 analysed by Aoki 2017.
  The age SD of 13 years used in the virtual cohort is assumed.
* **Drug effect.** The candidate dose-effect functions have no AZD1981
  estimates. The bootstrap result files in the paper's electronic
  supplementary material belong to the worked R example of the averaging
  method, not to an estimate on the trial data. No drug-effect term is
  packaged.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for Aoki 2017 was found in Europe PMC as
  of 2026-11-25.
